title: AI Consumption Assessment
framing: This is an analysis of how the publication layer's structured data would be read by different classes of machine consumer, grounded in the evidence gathered in AQ-04A-D and AQ-04F (schema-inventory.json, ontology-mapping verification, relationship-semantics review, jsonld-coverage.json, schema-validation.json) — not a new set of measurements. No consumer-specific schema variants were added; the same JSON-LD serves every consumer class.

google_search_rich_results.eligible_rich_result_types: None claimed. WebPage/BreadcrumbList/DefinedTerm/DefinedTermSet/CollectionPage/Taxon/PropertyValue are all valid, low-risk, general-purpose types — none of them unlock a special SERP rich result (that would require Recipe, Product, FAQPage, etc., none of which accurately describe an educational reference entry). Not claiming eligibility this content doesn't have is itself a Rule 4 (omit rather than misrepresent) outcome, not a gap.
google_search_rich_results.breadcrumb_rich_result: Eligible and low-risk: BreadcrumbList is present on 100% of leaf/group/category pages (1,252/1,252), position sequences verified contiguous with no gaps (reports/schema-validation.json), every item an absolute canonical URL.
google_search_rich_results.impact_of_aq04b_fix: The description property (now the authored seo_description, 100% coverage) is a plausible meta-description/snippet source. The generic template it replaced ("Abondance (Natural Rind) — Cheeses cheese") was low-information and, at scale across near-identical group/category names, would read as templated to any quality classifier — the exact AI-content-detection risk this audit chain has flagged repeatedly in the wine-education tier. The authored replacement ("Abondance is a natural rind cow's milk cheese from FR (PDO).") is specific and non-templated.

google_knowledge_graph.signal_strength: Modest but structurally sound: stable @id per entity, DefinedTerm.identifier matching the governed catalog canonical id (verified 0/1,252 mismatches, reports/schema-inventory.json + ontology-mapping verification), consistent inDefinedTermSet per-domain grouping, and a verified-accurate isPartOf/hasPart hierarchy (0/2,354 issues across leaf isPartOf and group/category hasPart checks combined).
google_knowledge_graph.critical_fix: Before AQ-04B, 204 cheese pages asserted `{"@type": "Taxon", "name": "Bos taurus", "url": ".../cheeses/abondance/"}` — a direct, machine-readable claim that the URL's subject IS the species Bos taurus (cattle), contradicting the same page's own DefinedTerm identity (Abondance, food.cheese.natural-rind.abondance). A knowledge graph ingesting both statements about the same URL would either drop one as contradictory or, worse, conflate the cheese entity with the cattle-species entity. This was a real entity-identity integrity risk specific to machine consumers — a human reader would never misread the page this way, but a KG builder reading only the JSON-LD could have. Fixed: cheese pages now emit zero Taxon blocks; the milk-source fact is preserved as a PropertyValue, which does not assert subject identity.

ai_overviews_and_llm_browsing_chatgpt_cl.primary_consumption_path: These systems predominantly extract rendered text and meta tags when browsing/citing a page, with JSON-LD as a secondary structured signal when crawled for indexing. The AQ-04B description fix improves both paths identically, since <meta name="description"> and every JSON-LD description property now draw from the same authored narrative.seo_description field — there is exactly one source of truth for 'what is this page about' machine-readable text now, rather than a templated meta description and a differently-templated (but equally generic, pre-fix) JSON-LD description.
ai_overviews_and_llm_browsing_chatgpt_cl.entity_disambiguation: DefinedTerm.identifier (a stable, namespaced canonical id like food.cheese.natural-rind.abondance) gives an LLM building a retrieval index a consistent key to de-duplicate against on repeat crawls — verified globally unique across all 11 domains (4,460 distinct @id values, 0 collisions).
ai_overviews_and_llm_browsing_chatgpt_cl.residual_ambiguity_relevant_here: AQ-03's canonical-identity audit (reports/catalog-canonical-identity.json) surfaced 8 unresolved variety-pair candidates (e.g. mandarin/clementine/tangerine/satsuma) where the catalog treats visually/culinarily similar entities as separate canonical IDs. This is a catalog-layer question, not a publication-layer defect, and AQ-04 does not resolve it (out of scope, per Rule 1) — but it is worth naming here because an LLM assembling a knowledge graph from these pages would inherit that same unresolved ambiguity: is 'clementine' a distinct entity from 'mandarin,' or the same fact represented twice? The JSON-LD is faithfully projecting an catalog-level open question, not introducing a new one.

general_search_engines.assessment: Standard well-formed JSON-LD (@context, @type, absolute URLs, no orphaned @id references — verified via reports/schema-validation.json, 4,718/4,718 objects, 0 issues) with no exotic or deprecated vocabulary. No special accommodation needed or made for any specific engine; schema.org's shared vocabulary is engine-agnostic by design, and this layer doesn't fork behavior per consumer.

cross_cutting_qualities.clarity: Improved directly by AQ-04B (authored descriptions replace generic templates) and indirectly by AQ-04C (verified-accurate hierarchy means a consumer following isPartOf/hasPart lands on the right entity, not a stale or drifted one).
cross_cutting_qualities.consistency: Verified deterministic regeneration across all 11 domains (reports/*-schema-generation-report.json, "Deterministic regeneration": "PASS") — repeated crawls see byte-identical structured data for unchanged content, which is itself a trust signal search/AI indexing pipelines weight (content that changes shape between crawls with no underlying change reads as unstable or auto-generated noise).
cross_cutting_qualities.determinism: Same as above — a build property, not a per-request one, so it holds for every consumer identically.
cross_cutting_qualities.entity_identity: Strengthened by the Taxon fix (removes a specific contradiction) and by AQ-04C's verified 1:1 mapping between every DefinedTerm/DefinedTermSet identifier and its catalog canonical id. Not fully closed: the 8 AQ-03 canonical-identity candidates remain an open catalog-layer question that necessarily surfaces in the publication layer too, since publication faithfully projects the catalog (Rule 1).

not_done_and_why.no_faq_or_howto_schema: The rendered FAQ sections (AQ-02A) are real, authored Q&A content and would technically qualify for FAQPage markup, but Google deprecated FAQPage rich-result eligibility for most sites in 2023 and reserves it for authoritative government/health sources — adding it now would be schema for a rich result this site cannot actually earn, closer to 'using a property because it exists' than to faithful representation. Omitted deliberately.
not_done_and_why.no_relationship_schema: See reports/semantic-integrity.json (AQ-04D section) for the full rationale — no schema.org property, correctly scoped to DefinedTerm, exists for the site's editorial/wine-pairing relationship types without either using the wrong domain/range or flattening distinct relationship types into an ambiguous generic one.
